P1.evidence: The best P1a in the batch by a distance. The setter's notes were read back at the open — 'I had a chat with Derek, so he kind of walked me through what's been going on in your life. And I think I got a pretty good picture, like a baseline stuff' — and then used three separate times as discovery scaffolding: 'from what I heard, he told me that you spent most of your 20s more in a bodybuilding style training, correct?', 'Derek mentioned to me that like the knowledge is a big deal for you', and 'Derek also mentioned to me that you've tried some programs in the past, but eventually you hit a ceiling.' That is exactly what the check exists for and the prospect visibly felt seen. The frame carried two of four parts and no agreement was sought. Worth flagging separately for coaching: roughly eleven minutes of rapport on time zones, Poland, Seattle weather, snowboarding and Patagonia ran before any real discovery began.

P2.evidence: Five clean hits. Height and weight were both actually asked, which happened on only one other call in this batch — 'You look like a tall guy. How tall are you?' and 'Okay, and how much do you weigh?' — though age was never asked and remains unknown. Work established including the remote and flexible schedule. Injuries asked properly and followed up: 'What's up with the hips? Is there anything flaring up?' then 'Apart from the hips, do you feel anything that's limiting your movements?' Training week covered in real detail. Results from current training asked well — 'How did you feel about transitioning into more functional movements?' — drawing 'Incredible. I was like, I should have been doing this for 10 years.' Diet walked through fully with timing, hunger, snacking and the kryptonite question. The two misses are the same two as everywhere else: sleep and daytime energy were never asked. Wake time surfaced only as an input to the eating window. Health conditions were never asked at all — no medications, no bloodwork, no diagnoses — which matters given what the injury question turned up.

P3.evidence: The weakest goals phase in the batch. The physical layer was covered competently — 'tell me more about your goals. So, like, the physical stuff' produced hips, shoulders, legs, grip and the ready-for-anything frame — and that is where it stopped. No aesthetics question was ever asked and no appearance goal exists in this record. The bridge question was never asked, so the call never left the physical for a single moment. Nobody asked who else this impacts, and as a result the prospect's family status is completely unknown after 47 minutes. No reflect-back was attempted at any point. Longevity and identity did surface — the grip-strength studies, and the prospect's own 'I made a promise to myself years ago... that I'll always be in shape the rest of my life' — but both arrived through rapport rather than through the phase, and the twenty-year promise, which is the single strongest emotional asset in the call, was never picked up or used.

P4.evidence: Ran largely on the setter's groundwork. Past attempts arrived via Derek rather than being asked, but the rep opened the outcome properly — 'you've tried some programs in the past, but eventually you hit a ceiling kind of thing' — and the prospect elaborated. The blocker question was asked, if with a leading suggestion attached: 'Apart from the knowledge, do you feel anything else was missing? Like, I don't know, accountability part?' It worked, and the prospect then named the gap precisely and in his own words: 'I've never been great at planning workouts. I kind of just go in and work on what's like not sore', and 'the accountability of like actually planning out what I'm doing that day rather than just kind of winging it. So that's a big one.' He also drew the useful distinction himself, that his accountability problem is planning rather than turning up — 'as far as doing it every day, that's no problem.' P4f is scored a miss but would have been the wrong move here anyway: this prospect's own diagnosis is that information genuinely is the problem.

P5.evidence: Never run, in any form. No two-year projection, no settle question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. Six calls into this batch the consequence frame has not been attempted once. Here there was an obvious hook the rep raised himself and then walked away from — the grip-strength and get-up-off-the-floor longevity markers — which could have carried directly into what the next twenty years look like if the ceiling never breaks.

P6.evidence: A fit check ran rather than the scripted belief question: 'Do you feel like this checks all the boxes for you when it comes to your goals that you want to reach?' It drew an emphatic answer — 'Absolutely. Like this is, this is, yeah, that's the reason I finally reached out' — so P6c is satisfied, there was a clear yes before price and no hesitation to return to Phase 5 for. The all-in question was never asked.

P11.evidence: None of the four steps completed. The $6,000 was not collected — the only money taken was a $100 refundable deposit to hold a follow-up slot, and the Pava financing application had not returned when the call ended ('It hasn't come through yet'). No onboarding call with Trevor was booked; the slot taken was another call with the rep two hours later. No agreement was sent, mentioned or signed. No welcome email, no Skool invitation, no onboarding questionnaire. The prospect also had to leave for another meeting, which the rep accommodated. A ready, solvent, enthusiastic buyer finished the call owning nothing but a pending credit application.

objection_plays.detail: The trigger was soft — 'we could just split it up over the course of the six months' — from a buyer who moments later said '6K is totally doable for me'. This is the only call in twelve files where any part of the financial picture actually ran: 'What's your credit score?' It is a scripted move and it produced real information, an 800 score and debt-free status. Everything around it was skipped. No isolation before touching money, no should-versus-how frame, no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no card count, no used-versus-available, no investments. And the answer was used backwards: an 800 score and no debt is the strongest possible evidence that this buyer could simply pay, and the rep responded by recommending a 12-month external credit product at roughly $7,200. The 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up' line never appeared; financing was volunteered before the prospect had asked for anything beyond a split.
No think-about-it trigger. The prospect had been following the coach's content for a long time and had already decided to reach out.
No spouse-consult trigger. Family status was never established either way.
No timing objection. The prospect noted his heavy week had already passed — 'thankfully, that was two weeks ago. I think I'm safe for a while.'
No fear or doubt about the programme. He had pre-qualified the coach himself against every other creator in the category.

SCRIPT GAP — the clinical gate, again. The prospect described sharp recurring pain on the outside of the left hip radiating to the top of the left foot, with no diagnosis and a guess that it might be circulatory. The rep asked the screening question well but the playbook gives him nothing to do with the answer, so the disclosure was absorbed into the mobility pitch and no clearance was suggested. Worse, the vacuum was filled with the rep's own medical anecdote about being advised to have a hip replacement and avoiding it through kettlebells, delivered to a man with undiagnosed hip pain. A mandatory clearance step in P2d would have caught this.

SCRIPT GAP — the $100 refundable calendar deposit, appearing for the second time in this batch and paid this time. There is no scripted support for it, so the rep justified it with improvised scarcity: 'we're freaking packed with calendars. So when I'm booking in, I'm like, you know, kicking someone out. So I just need to take like a refundable deposit.' It secured the follow-up but it is an unbudgeted commitment device standing in for a close that P11 should have completed on the call. The principal should decide whether this instrument is sanctioned; it is currently being invented per-call.

notes: Strong front half, absent back half. P1a was exemplary and P2 collected height and weight for once, but P3 never left the physical, P5 did not run at all, and P11 scored zero — the buyer left with a pending credit application and a $100 deposit instead of a programme. The specific coaching point is the credit-score exchange: an 800 score with no debt from someone who just said $6,000 is doable is a signal to ask for the card, not to open a 12-month loan at $7,200. Separately, the rep must stop offering his own hip-replacement story as evidence to prospects who have disclosed undiagnosed joint pain.
